messages:
ella_support: getting multiple support tickets about 502s + timeouts to hosted inference in eu-west-2 since ~08:42 UTC. customers: two startup accounts + one enterprise. spike in API 5xx rate on the frontend gateway. triage please.
kevin_ops: seeing elevated 504s on the gateway logs too, spike aligns with 08:41:50 UTC. frontend -> edge -> egress shows retransmits.
rana_net: I ran an mtr from the eu-west-2a host to the edge egress IP, results show consistent packet loss starting at the provider hop (AS64500). snippet:
```
Start: 2026-03-15 08:45:02
HOST: i-0abcdef
 1.|-- 10.0.1.1        0.0%   0.4ms
 2.|-- 100.64.1.2      0.0%   0.7ms
 3.|-- 203.0.113.5    35.0%  12.5ms  <--- provider transit
 4.|-- 203.0.113.6    40.0%  13.1ms
 5.|-- edge.example   0.0%   14.0ms
```

This looks like an egress path flap at provider hop. tagging @carrier-noc-bot.
bryan_sre: confirmed correlated increase in session establishment timeouts and KV cache misses around same interval. latency SLO alerts firing.
tim_support: customer-facing: several users saw "502 Bad Gateway" or request timeout after ~10s. One customer posted logs with x-redwood-request-id: rwd_9f8a2. They're asking for ETA and credits.
ella_support: please collect repro steps for support. ask customers to run `curl -v` and include x-redwood-request-id. also capture traceroute.
kevin_ops: repro from a synthetic probe in eu-west-2a -> hosted inference endpoint: `curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" --max-time 10` returns 502 with upstream read timeout. Gateway logs show upstream 504 from edge at 08:42:10.
rana_net: I pushed a temporary route via our backup IX peer in eu-west-2 (announce via BGP community no-export workaround) to steer egress away from the flaky provider. monitoring now.
infra-bot: automated note: BGP path change initiated by rana_net at 08:54 UTC.
bryan_sre: after reroute I'm seeing 5xx rate drop to baseline in eu-west-2 within 90s. synthetic success rate improved from 85% -> 99% in the checks.
tim_support: updated customers: told them we identified an upstream provider path issue, rerouted traffic, continuing to monitor. asked about credits -> propose 10% usage credit for impacted window.
kevin_ops: filing post-incident ticket with provider: attaching mtr + pcap. ran tcpdump on egress host capturing retransmits and duplicate acks to provider hop. small pcap attached to ticket.
carrier-noc-bot: thanks. carrier NOC case #CN-83421 created. they report a partial interface error and are investigating.
ella_support: once carrier confirms, we'll draft postmortem + remediation steps. immediate remediation: 1) keep backup BGP path for eu-west-2 egress for 48h, 2) add provider health probe to route selection, 3) update runbook for supported failover.
rana_net: agreed. also adding automated prefix blackhole detection to avoid oscillation (will test in staging).
bryan_sre: note for follow-up: validate canary traffic policy to prefer intra-az paths when inter-az cross-connect latency > 30ms. edge cases where cross-zone egress increases tail latency.
tim_support: logging out: customers asked for exact window and request ids. I exported request ids for 08:41:30 -> 08:56:00 for billing/credits.
ella_support: closing loop: incident root cause = provider egress interface partial outage causing packet loss and BGP path instability -> gateway upstream read timeouts -> API 5xx/timeouts for hosted inference in eu-west-2. mitigation = temporary BGP reroute to backup IX, traffic steering, customer credits offered. next steps: postmortem + provider SLA claim.
kevin_ops: I'll schedule a follow-up postmortem meeting at 15:00 UTC to run through telemetry and remediation.
ella_support: thanks all. if carrier NOC updates, drop here. :thumbsup:
carrier-noc-bot: carrier update 09:20 UTC: cleared faulty interface; BGP paths stable. recommend keep backup peer on for 24h.
ella_support: noted. will keep incident open for 24h and then file postmortem.
